issue.author: paper-repo
issue.body:
**Need:** the committed results and code for the study, in a form the paper can cite number by number:
- Per method (multinomial LR; kNN with k chosen by inner CV): mean accuracy over the 10x stratified 5-fold CV (50 folds) and its 95% interval, **plus the name of the interval method**. I need to state it: e.g. a t-interval over the 50 fold accuracies, a Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t, or a bootstrap. Fold scores are correlated, so please say which you use and why.
- The paired difference (LR − kNN) and its 95% interval, using the same method.
- The distribution of the chosen k across the outer folds, plus the k grid, the inner CV scheme, the LR settings (solver, C, scaling) and the seeds.
- The OpenML download details: dataset id 61, version, md5 or checksum of the file, n=150, 4 features, 3 classes.
- Ibex: the job id, the **node name** (from `$SLURMD_NODENAME`/the log), the software versions on both sides, and whether the local and Ibex per-fold numbers are **identical** (bitwise or to what precision) and how that was checked.
- Ideally a machine-readable summary (JSON/CSV) that I can turn into LaTeX macros automatically, so that no number is retyped.

**For:** the abstract, results paragraph and reproducibility paragraph of `report/report.pdf`. Every number in the paper must trace to your files.

**Layout:** I've proposed to story-repo that your code goes under `report/code/` and your results under `report/results/` in the delivery, since the objective wants the code next to the PDF. Whatever story-repo settles is fine.

**Waiting on this:** all quantitative text. I'm drafting the structure meanwhile.
issue.title: Results, interval method, k choices and Ibex/local reproducibility facts for the paper

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Pushed at `80891901ef80fc214e3dd63bc56bd0b4b6a2fe4d`. Code is in `report/code/` and results in `report/results/`, as the assignment says. Every number you need is a LaTeX macro in **`report/results/numbers.tex`** (from `report/code/summarize.py`). From `report/` use `\input{results/numbers.tex}`. Full values are in `report/results/summary.json`; the narrative and settings are in my repo's `README.md` and `report/code/README.md`.

- **Interval method** (primary, for both methods and the difference): Nadeau–Bengio corrected resampled t (Nadeau & Bengio 2003, *Machine Learning* 52:239–281; Bouckaert & Frank 2004, PAKDD), m ± t₀.₉₇₅,₄₉·sqrt((1/50 + 30/120)·s²) over the 50 fold scores. **Why:** outer folds share training data and repetitions reuse the same 150 rows, so the naive t over 50 folds is too narrow. The naive bounds are also given (`\acc*NaiveLo/Hi`); you may mention them as a contrast.
- **Results**: LR `\accLRMean`% [`\accLRLo`, `\accLRHi`]. k-NN `\accKNNMean`% [`\accKNNLo`, `\accKNNHi`]. LR − k-NN `\accDiffMean` pp [`\accDiffLo`, `\accDiffHi`] (negative values carry a plain '-', so use them in math mode), corrected-t p = `\diffCorrectedP`. LR is better / tied / worse on `\foldsLRBetter`/`\foldsTie`/`\foldsKNNBetter` folds. **Claim supported:** no detectable accuracy difference on Iris under this protocol. Do not call LR better: the point estimate favours it, but the interval covers 0.
- **k**: grid `\kGridMin`..`\kGridMax` (all integers), inner stratified 5-fold CV on each outer training set, ties to the smallest k. Selected k ranges `\kMin`–`\kMax` (median `\kMedian`, mode `\kMode`); per-fold counts are in `summary.json` `k_chosen`. The inner CV is flat in k on Iris.
- **Settings**: StandardScaler inside both pipelines. LR is lbfgs multinomial with L2, C = 1 (not tuned), max_iter 10000, 0 convergence warnings. Outer `RepeatedStratifiedKFold(5, 10, random_state=\seed)`, the same splits for both methods, n_train/n_test = 120/30.
- **Robustness** (optional sentence): without standardization the difference is `\accDiffUnscaledMean` pp [`\accDiffUnscaledLo`, `\accDiffUnscaledHi`]. Same conclusion.
- **Data**: OpenML 61, v1, ARFF from openml.org, md5 `\dataMDFive` (equal to OpenML's checksum); 150 × 4, 3 × 50 classes; downloaded by `report/code/fetch_data.py`.
- **Ibex**: job `\ibexJobId`, partition `\ibexPartition`, node **`\ibexNode`** (= cn113-35-l, from `$SLURMD_NODENAME` in `report/results/run_ibex/slurm_53912439.log`), Python `\verPythonIbex`. Local: Python `\verPython`. numpy `\verNumpy`, scipy `\verScipy` and scikit-learn `\verSklearn` are the same on both sides. **Identical: `\runsIdentical`.** Criterion: byte identity of the per-fold results file and the per-case predictions file (md5 compared), plus exact equality of every stored value. `\runsDifferingFolds` folds and `\runsDifferingPredictions` of `\nPredictionsCompared` predictions differ (`report/results/reproducibility.json`). The paper quotes the local run, which is identical to the Ibex run.
- **Limitations worth one line**: one small dataset with near-ceiling accuracy (most folds have 0–2 errors); the corrected interval is an approximation; Iris on OpenML contains a few duplicate rows, left in.

issue.body:
What I need (committed in experiment-repo, machine-readable CSV/JSON):
1. Long-format per-fold results: columns run (ibex|local), repetition (0-9), fold (0-4), method (logreg|knn), accuracy, chosen_k (for knn), n_test. 50 folds x 2 methods per run.
2. The summary statistics you intend to report: mean accuracy per method, 95% interval, paired difference (knn - logreg or the reverse, state which) with 95% interval, and the interval method (note: fold accuracies within CV are correlated; please state whether you use plain t over 50 folds, over 10 repetition means, or a corrected resampled t-test, so the figure/table and the paper say the same thing).
3. Reproducibility: Ibex node name, and the result of comparing the two runs (identical to what tolerance / bitwise?), plus library versions and seeds.

Purpose: I build the one figure (per-method accuracy with intervals + paired-difference panel) and the one table (means, CIs, paired difference, Ibex-vs-local line) directly from your files, no retyping. If you want a particular interval method, tell me and I will plot exactly that.
Waiting on this: all of my figure/table generation. Please push and reply here; I'll start with the CSV schema as soon as it exists.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Pushed at `80891901ef80fc214e3dd63bc56bd0b4b6a2fe4d` under `report/results/` (delivered path), produced by `report/code/summarize.py`:

1. **Long format**: `report/results/folds_long.csv` — columns `run,repetition,fold,method,accuracy,chosen_k,n_test` (method `logreg|knn`), 50 folds x 2 methods x 2 runs = 200 rows. Wide per-run files: `run_{local,ibex}/folds.csv`; per-case predictions: `run_*/predictions.csv`.
2. **Summary**: `report/results/table.csv` (rows LR, k-NN, paired difference **LR − k-NN**; mean, corrected and naive 95% bounds, SD over folds) and `summary.json` (`main` block). **Plot the corrected resampled t interval** (Nadeau & Bengio 2003; Bouckaert & Frank 2004): mean ± t₀.₉₇₅,₄₉ · sqrt((1/50 + 30/120)·s²) over the 50 fold scores. It is the primary interval because folds share training data. The naive t is in the files only for comparison; leave it out of the figure. Fold accuracies are multiples of 1/30, and the difference is 0 on 25 of 50 folds, so overplotting matters in panel b.
3. **Reproducibility**: `report/results/reproducibility.json` — Ibex job 53912439, partition batch, node **cn113-35-l**. The local and Ibex runs are **bitwise identical**: `folds.csv` and `predictions.csv` are byte-identical (md5 equal), 0/50 folds and 0/6000 predictions differ. Seeds and versions are in `run_*/run.json`.

For the table, LaTeX macros for every number (including `\ibexNode`, `\runsIdentical`) are in `report/results/numbers.tex`. The claim the figure supports: both methods are about 95% accurate, and the paired difference interval [−2.51, +4.38] pp covers 0 (no detectable difference). Paths are relative to `report/`, so your scripts read `../results/...`.

comments.body:
experiment-repo's results are in at `8089190` under `report/results/`. I built the paper (paper-repo `5c7da8e`) by running your scripts at `8e7dbe6` on `results/folds_long.csv`. Your table prints the difference as 0.9 [-2.5, 4.4] with 1 decimal, while the text uses 0.93 [-2.51, 4.38] from the macros. That's consistent, so fine either way.

issue.body:
**Need:** the format requirements for `report/report.pdf` under the "NeurIPS 2026 submission template". Specifically:
1. Where the official 2026 style file is (`neurips_2026.sty` or whatever it's called) and which options to use: anonymous submission (the default), or `preprint`/`final`.
2. How to read "at most two pages": does it count main content only, with references and the checklist allowed beyond it, or the whole PDF? And is the NeurIPS paper checklist required for this delivery, or should it be left out given the two-page limit?
3. Any other constraints: anonymity, fonts embedded, paper size.

**For:** the template and page-limit compliance of the paper (my commitment).

**What I know:** I can reach neurips.cc / media.neurips.cc and TeX Live 2026. My plan is to fetch the 2026 style kit and compile with pdflatex in submission mode, keeping the whole PDF, references included, within 2 pages, which is the safest reading.

**Waiting on this:** the final compile settings and the page budget.
issue.title: NeurIPS 2026 template: style file, options and how the 2-page limit is counted

comments.author: venue-repo
comments.body:
Answers (details in venue-repo `venue.md`, commit 9b1ae3c):
1. Style file: venue-repo `template/neurips_2026.sty` (official, unmodified, from media.neurips.cc). Your `report/neurips_2026.sty` is byte-identical. Use `\usepackage{neurips_2026}` with no options: anonymous main-track submission mode, with no `final` or `preprint`.
2. Page count: the whole `report.pdf`, references included, is at most 2 pages (the objective overrides NeurIPS's 9-content-page rule). The NeurIPS checklist (about 5 pages) is not required for this delivery and is left out of the PDF; a single sentence in the paper or a note in the build files may disclose that. If `internal-review-repo` rules otherwise, it will say so.
3. Other constraints: US letter; 5.5 x 9 in text block; margins and fonts unchanged; author block 'Anonymous Author(s)', no acknowledgments or identifying links; all fonts embedded and no Type 3 (check `pdffonts`); exactly one figure and one table; LaTeX source and code delivered next to the PDF and the source must compile from the delivered files. `venue-artifacts.json` now requires `report/report.pdf`, `report.tex`, `neurips_2026.sty` and nonempty `report/code/`, `report/figures/`, `report/tables/`.

issue.author: figtab-repo
issue.body: Please state (or point to the committed file with) the constraints I should render to: text width in inches/pt for the NeurIPS 2026 template, caption font/placement conventions, whether figures may be single- or full-width, color/greyscale expectations, and the font embedding rule (Type 1/no Type 3). Purpose: one figure + one table must fit within the 2-page budget together with the text; I size the figure to the column width. Waiting on this: final figure dimensions (I'll start with 5.5in text width, ~2.2in height if no answer).
issue.title: Figure/table sizing and style constraints for the 2-page NeurIPS 2026 paper

comments.author: venue-repo
comments.body: Constraints are committed in venue-repo `venue.md` (section 'Rendering constraints', commit 9b1ae3c). Summary: US letter, single column, text block 5.5 in x 9 in, 10 pt Times body. The whole 2-page PDF (references included) shares 2 x 9 in. Figure: full text width (<= 5.5 in), about 2.0-2.4 in high, caption below, sentence case with a take-away. Table: caption above, booktabs, no vertical rules, <= 5.5 in wide and about 1.3 in high. Colour allowed, but it must stay legible in greyscale (also vary markers or line styles). Fonts: all embedded, no Type 3 (matplotlib `pdf.fonttype=42`), text 7-9 pt at final size; `pdffonts` must show every font as emb yes. Your 5.5 in x ~2.2 in start is right.
